title: Expire temporary fields
summary: A TTL gives written values a time to live.
introduction: A TTL gives written values a time to live. Your task: Read the TTL twice a few seconds apart.
learningObjectives: Read the TTL twice a few seconds apart.
Explain the example for expire temporary fields

blocks.text: A TTL gives written values a time to live. Cassandra removes them from ordinary reads after they expire.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code:
INSERT INTO reading_by_reader(reader_id,day,title,pages) VALUES('temporary-reader','2026-11-16','Practice',1) USING TTL 60;
SELECT TTL(title) FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='temporary-reader' AND day='2026-11-16';
blocks.title: Expire temporary fields

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `TTL` reports remaining life in seconds. Its result changes as time passes and uses special values for missing or non-expiring keys.
`USING TTL` gives written CQL values a lifetime measured in seconds.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The TTL value is near 60 seconds when read immediately and decreases with time.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Expiration creates deletion work that is cleaned up later. A TTL is not a free way to ignore data-lifecycle planning.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Read the TTL twice a few seconds apart.
